title: The soul and body (ST I.76)
hookLine: the soul is the form of the body, not a ghost in a machine

cards: "I'm stuck in this body." People say it on a bad back day, in a hospital gown, at the end of a long shift.
The picture behind it: the real you is somewhere inside, a pilot at the controls, and the body is the machine you drive. A modern phrase calls this a ghost in a machine.
Thomas Aquinas knew an older version of the picture, and in the Summa he takes it apart. Today: the soul and body, and why they aren't two things.

teach.b: Thomas's key word is form: what makes a thing the kind of thing it is, from the inside. An image of our own may help. Clay shaped into a cup isn't clay plus an invisible cup riding along.

The shape is what makes this clay a cup. Thomas says the soul is the form of the body in a deeper way: it's what makes this matter alive, and human, and you. So the soul isn't parked in the head, steering.
It's whole in the whole body, and whole in each part. On this view, your hands aren't tools you operate. They are you, reaching.
And a person doesn't have one soul for growing, another for feeling and a third for thinking.
One soul does it all. The you that digests lunch is the you that prays. Genesis tells it with dust and breath.
In the Douay-Rheims: "the Lord God formed man of the slime of the earth: and breathed into his face the breath of life, and man became a living soul." Not breath dropped into a container.
Earth and breath, one living thing. Thomas holds that the human soul is spiritual and outlives death. But in his commentary on First Corinthians, he says a separated soul is not the whole person.
It's one reason the Creed speaks of the resurrection of the body, not an escape from it: back on day three hundred twenty-nine, the body too.
And Paul, in the Douay-Rheims, can ask: "know you not, that your members are the temple of the Holy Ghost". On Thomas's account, the body isn't packaging. It's part of the person God made.

how: Catholics profess belief in the resurrection of the body in the Creed, and Catholic teaching describes the soul as the form of the body, so that body and soul together make one human nature.

games.q: what does “the soul and body” mean?
o: the soul as the form that makes a body alive
a spirit riding inside a body like a pilot
two parts that split for good at death

p: what makes a thing the kind it is
slime of the earth, breath of life

games.q: you're Thomas. a student says: the real me is my soul, and my body is a machine I drive. what do you answer?
o: agree: the body is only the vehicle.
say the soul is the form of the body, so body and soul are one person.
say there's no soul, only the body.
games.why: Thomas calls the soul the form of the body: what makes this matter a living human. not a pilot, and not nothing.

practice: Move your attention slowly up from your feet, legs, belly, chest, hands, shoulders, jaw, eyes, treating each place not as equipment but as yourself.
Where you find strain or tiredness, do one small kind thing for it right now: unclench, stretch, let it rest. If you pray, thank God for one part of you that has served you well.

wordCard.voice: The soul and body. For Thomas, the soul is the body's form, what makes it alive and human: one person, not a ghost in a machine. Today's words.

orig.note: Latin, the language Thomas wrote in: the soul, the form of the body.

carryVoice: Your line: you are one. Your body is you, not your vehicle. Go gently.
